Based on my photon Monte Carlo transport (2.2M source photons in the 30 cm water cube, 10×10 cm² SSD-100 Co-60-like beam), analytic weighting of the scored photon fluence spectra with cross sections and Klein–Nishina kinematics for interactions/initial electrons, and a CSDA slowing-down spectrum with Møller knock-on (Spencer–Fano) for the electron layer, I obtained the following best estimates. At 5 cm depth the absorbed dose is taken equal to collision kerma (electron equilibrium, β ≈ 1); PDD is from the central-axis collision-kerma depth curve.

  "method": "Photon MC (2.2M source photons) in 30 cm water cube, 10x10 cm2 SSD-100 Co-60-like beam; fluences scored as track length/volume in the r=1 cm, 0.2 cm cylinder at 5 cm, normalized to Phi0=1/(4pi*105^2). Compton sampled with Klein-Nishina, Rayleigh treated as forward-elastic, photoelectric/pair absorbed. L2/L3 obtained by weighting the scored photon fluence spectra with interaction cross sections (primary lines at 1.1732/1.3325 MeV) and KN electron kinematics. Electron layer from CSDA slowing-down spectra with Møller knock-ons (delta rays). Dose = collision kerma (CPE, beta=1); kerma from mass energy-transfer/absorption coefficients; PDD from depth-dose Kcol curve (dmax~0.5 cm); s_w,air taken as standard 60Co Spencer-Attix value.",
